name: Excel V laser
lead: Excel V is a vascular and pigment laser made by Cutera. It combines a 532-nm green laser (KTP-type, frequency-doubled Nd:YAG) with a 1064-nm Nd:YAG, and is used in clinics for redness, visible blood vessels, port-wine stains and pigment such as lentigines.[1][2]

Published studies are small. A prospective study in 5 adults used a short-pulse 532-nm Nd:YAG (Excel V) for port-wine stains[1], a randomised open-label study compared 532-nm KTP and 595-nm pulsed dye lasers for erythematous surgical scars[3], and registered Cutera studies include rosacea, lentigines on the hands and poikiloderma of Civatte.[4][5][6]

paras: The 532-nm wavelength is absorbed by haemoglobin and melanin, and the 1064-nm wavelength penetrates deeper. Registered Cutera studies list port-wine stain, rosacea, lentigines, spider angioma, scarring and skin ageing.[1][2][4][5][7]

A prospective, controlled study of five adults reported on short-pulse 532-nm Nd:YAG for port-wine stains.[1] A randomised comparison of 532-nm KTP and 595-nm pulsed dye laser for erythematous surgical scars is a related study of the same wavelength family, not specific to Excel V.[3] Registered studies include a 24-participant poikiloderma study, a 15-participant rosacea study combining 532-nm KTP and 1064-nm laser, a 24-participant study on hand lentigines and a 22-participant spider angioma study.[4][5][6][7] Results are not summarised in the registry entries cited here.

card.note: Professional device; evidence is small studies.

quick.overview:
Excel V is a Cutera clinic laser with a green 532-nm and an infrared 1064-nm wavelength. It is used for redness, small vessels, port-wine stains and brown spots.

Studies naming it are small, often a handful to a couple of dozen patients.
quick.mechanism: Green light is absorbed by blood and pigment; the 1064-nm light reaches deeper vessels. Heat closes small vessels or breaks up pigment.
quick.risks: Adverse effects are not summarised in the registry entries reviewed; vascular lasers in general may cause bruising or pigment change. Clinic-only.
